title: SAP Retail Signal
body:
Fitting-room interest.
Unavailable online sizes.
Supply-chain response.
narration: SAP Retail Signal connects fitting-room interest, unavailable online sizes, and supply-chain response in one product.

title: 1 · Smart fitting-room signals
callout: Joule highlights the gap and asks Bob to check availability, fit and price.
narration: First, fitting-room signals. The cream medium top has two hundred forty try-ons but forty-three purchases. Jewel highlights low conversion and available stock. Bob investigates availability, fit and price; the signal cannot establish the cause.

title: 2 · Out-of-stock demand tracker
body:
162 qualified sessions
× 15% assumed conversion
= 24 scenario units
callout: Joule helps Bob test a restock quantity, then checks stock and lead time.
narration: Second, online demand. One hundred sixty-two qualified out-of-stock sessions suggest twenty-four units at an assumed fifteen-percent conversion rate. Jewel helps test that restock quantity against stock and lead time. These are possible purchases, not confirmed orders.

title: 3 · Supply-chain risk and response
eyebrow: SELECT AN INPUT · SEE ITS CONTEXT
body:
Natural gas
CAD 5.80 per MMBtu
at Pacific Apparel
callout: Supplier purchase rates and public market benchmarks stay separate.
narration: Third, supply-chain risk. Bob selects natural gas to inspect suppliers, purchase rates and a dated market benchmark. Contract prices and public benchmarks stay separate.

title: A gas shortage reaches the network
body:
25% less new supply
30% higher input price
7 additional delivery days
callout: The graph highlights exposed products, production and fulfillment.
narration: Bob simulates twenty-five percent less new supply, a thirty-percent input-price increase and seven extra delivery days. The graph highlights exposed products and facilities. Existing inventory stays available.

title: Joule explains cost and margin
body:
CAD 208 added cost
68.20% → 67.89% margin
329 planned units deferred
callout: Deferred production is not automatically permanently lost sales.
narration: Jewel explains about two hundred eight dollars added cost on completed new production. Weighted margin falls from sixty-eight point two to sixty-seven point eight nine percent. Three hundred twenty-nine planned units are deferred, not permanently lost.

title: Bob chooses an accountable response
body:
40 units transferred
CAD 60 modeled cost
10% → 60% coverage
callout: Receipt, not approval, makes stock sellable. All SAP and Joule actions here are simulated.
narration: Bob tests a forty-unit transfer costing sixty dollars. Seven-day coverage rises from ten to sixty percent. Approval, dispatch and receipt remain separate steps. SAP and Jewel connections here are simulated.
